> Turn a sample sheet and a model (factors with reference levels, covariates with units, batch, interactions, strata) into mzLib's design per stratum: the design matrix, its rank and aliased terms, the default contrasts with their estimability, and the design and contrast tables stats fit reads.

Wire verb `diff design` · Python [`pymzlib.diff.design`][pymzlib.diff.design]

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `samples` | `path` | required | — | — | The sample sheet: a TSV with a header row and one row per biological sample. The first column is the sample id (unique, any header). Every other column is available to the model by its header; a column the model does not name is ignored and listed in unused_columns. Cells are trimmed. A factor, stratum or batch cell is used as text, exactly as written. A covariate cell is a number in the covariate's stored unit; a blank, NA or NaN covariate cell is no value, and mzLib refuses that sample by name. |
| `stdin` | `string[]` | required | — | `one model term per line; fields tab-separated` | The model, one term per line, its fields separated by tabs; an empty optional field is not given, so mzLib's default applies. factor NAME, optionally then REFERENCE: a condition factor treatment-coded against REFERENCE (FactorSpec); with no REFERENCE every pair of its levels is compared and mzLib warns. covariate NAME UNIT, optionally then SCALE, SCALED_UNIT and CENTRE: a numeric column entered as (value - CENTRE) / SCALE (CovariateSpec). UNIT is the stored unit (years); SCALE is stored units per scaled unit (10), default 1; SCALED_UNIT names the unit a slope is per (decade), default SCALE stored units; CENTRE is in the stored unit, default the stratum's mean. interaction FIRST SECOND: the two-factor interaction of two named factors. stratum NAME: a column whose value splits the samples into strata, each designed on its own. batch NAME: the column holding each sample's batch, fitted as a fixed block whenever it is named (mzLib's DesignSpec.FitBatch default; the bridge never sets it). Factors and covariates enter in the order given. A column has one role, and is named once. |
| `out` | `path` | absent | — | — | A directory (created if absent) to write the pivot files into: for stratum i in the order of strata, design_i.tsv and, when any contrast is estimable there, contrasts_i.tsv. Files are numbered, not named by stratum key, because a key can hold any character a sheet cell can; each strata entry names its files. Files of the same name are overwritten. Absent, nothing is written. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `samples_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the sample sheet. |
| `sample_count` | `int` | samples | never | Samples read from the sheet, across every stratum. |
| `factors` | `object[]` | — | never | The factors given, in order: name and reference_level (null when none was given, so every pair of levels is compared). |
| `covariates` | `object[]` | — | never | The covariates given, in order: name, unit, and scale, scaled_unit and centre as given (each null when not given, so mzLib's default applied). |
| `interactions` | `object[]` | — | never | The interactions given, in order, each as first and second. |
| `stratum_columns` | `string[]` | — | never | The stratum columns given; empty for one stratum. |
| `batch_column` | `string` | — | yes: no batch line: batch is not in the model | The batch column given. |
| `unused_columns` | `string[]` | — | never | Sheet columns after the sample id that the model does not name, in sheet order. |
| `stratum_count` | `int` | strata | never | Designs built: one per distinct stratum key, or 1. |
| `strata` | `object[]` | — | never | One object per stratum, in mzLib's order (ordinal by stratum key); fields under result.tables.strata. |
| `estimability_counts` | `map<string,int>` | contrasts | never | Default contrasts per verdict across strata: estimable, not_estimable:confounded, not_estimable:rank_deficient. |
| `written` | `object` | — | yes: no --out: nothing was written | directory (absolute) and file_count, the design and contrast files written. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Default contrasts across strata: the table's row count. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns, in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per (stratum, default contrast): strata in order, each stratum's contrasts in mzLib's order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Five static caveats, plus one when any contrast is not estimable (with counts) and one when any stratum cannot run a contrast the model asks for. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stratum` | `string` | — | never | The stratum key (AnalysisDesign.StratumKey): the stratum columns sorted by name, each name=value, joined by ';', with %, ; and = in a value escaped as %25, %3B and %3D; all when there is no stratum column. |
| `contrast_id` | `string` | — | never | c1, c2, ... in mzLib's default order, numbered within the stratum. The name a contrasts file gives the contrast. |
| `label` | `string` | — | never | Readable: factor=level vs factor=reference for a level, the covariate's column name for a slope (age (per decade)). |
| `numerator` | `string` | — | yes: a slope | The numerator level as factor=level. |
| `denominator` | `string` | — | yes: a slope | The reference (or earlier) level as factor=level. |
| `covariate` | `string` | — | yes: not a slope | For a slope, the covariate. |
| `covariate_unit` | `string` | — | yes: not a slope | For a slope, the unit the effect is per: SCALED_UNIT, or SCALE stored units (10 years), or the stored unit at scale 1. |
| `covariate_scale` | `string` | — | yes: not a slope | For a slope, mzLib's statement of how the stored covariate became that unit, e.g. years/10, centred at 50 years. |
| `estimability` | `string` | — | never | mzLib's verdict: estimable \| not_estimable:confounded (the direction it needs is shared by two or more terms, e.g. a condition only ever in one batch) \| not_estimable:rank_deficient (it needs a column no sample informs, e.g. an empty interaction cell). Judged on the columns divided by their lengths, so the same in any unit. |
| `weights` | `float[]` | contrast weight per design column (unitless) | never | One weight per entry of the stratum's column_names: the contrast is the weighted sum of the coefficients. |
| `fitted_weights` | `float[]` | contrast weight per fitted column (unitless) | yes: not estimable: no fit gives it an estimate | AnalysisDesign.FittedWeights: the weights on the stratum's fitted_column_names, the row the contrasts file writes. A fit of the fitted matrix gives with them the estimate and standard error every least-squares fit of the full matrix gives. |

Fields of `strata`:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stratum` | `string` | — | never | The stratum key, as the table's stratum column. |
| `sample_count` | `int` | samples | never | Samples in the stratum. |
| `sample_ids` | `string[]` | — | never | The rows of matrix and of the design file, ordinal by sample id. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | mzLib's columns: intercept; factor=level for each non-reference level; batch=level; name (per unit) for a covariate; a=level:b=level for an interaction. |
| `fitted_column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | AnalysisDesign.FittedColumns by name: every column at full rank, else each column kept unless it is redundant with those kept before it. The design file's coefficient columns. |
| `rank` | `int` | columns | never | The numerical rank, by LinearModel's own full-rank test: the number of fitted columns. |
| `aliased_terms` | `string[]` | — | never | Terms (factor names, batch, covariate names, intercept) that share a direction with another term and so cannot be separated from it; empty at full rank. |
| `warnings` | `string[]` | — | never | What mzLib left out of the model or changed from the specification here, in plain words: a factor with one level, a reference level with no sample, one batch, no reference declared. |
| `not_run` | `object[]` | — | never | Contrasts the model asks for that this stratum cannot run, each with label and reason (not_in_stratum). |
| `covariate_centres` | `map<string,float>` | the covariate's stored unit | never | The centre subtracted from each covariate here: the one given, else the stratum's mean. |
| `matrix` | `float[][]` | coding (0/1 indicators; covariate columns in scaled units) | never | AnalysisDesign.Matrix, one row per sample_ids entry and one value per column_names entry. Equals R's stats::model.matrix for the same formula and level order. |
| `fitted_matrix` | `float[][]` | coding (0/1 indicators; covariate columns in scaled units) | never | AnalysisDesign.FittedMatrix: matrix with only the fitted columns. It has full column rank, so LinearModel.Fit takes it; it is the design file's body. |
| `design_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --out | Absolute path of design_i.tsv: header sample then fitted_column_names, then one row per sample, the fitted matrix in round-trip decimal. Exactly what stats fit --design reads. |
| `contrasts_file` | `string` | — | yes: no --out, or no contrast is estimable in this stratum | Absolute path of contrasts_i.tsv: header contrast then fitted_column_names (the design file's coefficient columns, same order), then one row per estimable contrast: contrast_id and fitted_weights. Each row is the ContrastWeights(name, weights) mzLib's EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts takes for a fit of the design file. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | --samples missing, blank or not found; --out given without a directory; the sheet empty, header-only, with an empty or repeated column name, an empty or repeated sample id (repeats across strata included), or a row whose field count differs from its header; a covariate cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN) |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | a stdin line that is not factor, covariate, interaction, stratum or batch, or has the wrong number of fields; an empty name or unit; a SCALE or CENTRE that is not a finite number; a column named twice or in two roles; a second batch line; an interaction given twice; a named column the sheet does not have |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a sample with no value for a factor or covariate, a non-positive scale, batch on some samples only, an interaction naming a factor that is not in the model |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- Each stratum's matrix is mzLib's AnalysisDesign: an intercept; each factor treatment-coded against its reference level, its other levels in ordinal order; batch against its first level; each covariate as (value - centre) / scale; then any interactions. It equals R's stats::model.matrix for the same formula and level order.
- Only mzLib's default contrasts are listed (AnalysisDesign.DefaultContrasts): each level against its factor's reference, every pair of levels when a factor has no reference, and each covariate's slope. With an interaction in the model, a factor's contrast is its effect at the reference level of the other factor.
- Contrast ids (c1, c2, ...) are numbered within each stratum, so one id can name different comparisons in two strata. Match contrasts across strata by label.
- A design file holds only the fitted columns (fitted_column_names): mzLib leaves out a column that is redundant with earlier ones, because LinearModel.Fit refuses a design without full column rank. A contrast that is not estimable has no fitted weights and is not in the contrasts file.
- Strata are never columns: each stratum gets its own design and nothing is shared between them. The individual a sample came from is never a fixed column either; it is for a mixed model's random intercept.

### Example

```python
design = pymzlib.diff.design('malat_dilution_samples.tsv', factors=[pymzlib.diff.FactorSpec('malat_load', '500ng')], out='malat_design')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`diff_design_malat.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/diff_design_malat.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
design = pymzlib.diff.design('design_factor_batch_covariate_samples.tsv', factors=[pymzlib.diff.FactorSpec('condition', 'ctrl')], covariates=[pymzlib.diff.CovariateSpec('age', 'years', scale=10, scaled_unit='decade', centre=50)], batch='batch')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`diff_design_factor_batch_covariate.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/diff_design_factor_batch_covariate.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
design = pymzlib.diff.design('design_confounded_samples.tsv', factors=[pymzlib.diff.FactorSpec('condition', 'A')], batch='batch')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`diff_design_confounded.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/diff_design_confounded.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
design = pymzlib.diff.design('stratified_samples.tsv', factors=[pymzlib.diff.FactorSpec('condition', 'A')], strata=['organism part'])
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`diff_design_strata.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/diff_design_strata.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

### References

- [doi:10.2307/2346786](https://doi.org/10.2307/2346786): the model-formula notation (main effects and a:b interactions) that R's stats::model.matrix implements and mzLib's design matrix equals (Wilkinson and Rogers, Appl Stat 22:392, 1973)

!!! warning "Not yet verified"

    - stats fit does not read a contrasts file yet (no --contrasts at this bridge). The file's pairing with mzLib is held directly: DifferentialTests.Design_TheContrastsFileIsWhatModerateContrastsTakes fits the design file with LinearModel.Fit and passes each row to EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts. Until stats fit takes it, a default contrast against a reference level is one coefficient (fitted_weights holds a single 1), which stats fit tests by its design column name.
    - Only DefaultContrasts is exposed. mzLib's AnalysisDesign.Between (any two levels) and Custom (weights by column name) have no wire form yet; with no reference declared, DefaultContrasts already gives every pair.
    - AnalysisSample.FromExperimentalDesign is not reachable: mzLib has no reader from MetaMorpheus's ExperimentalDesign.tsv to an IExperimentalDesign (MetaMorpheus's EngineLayer.ExperimentalDesign has one), so this verb starts from a sample sheet.
